speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation for acute diarrhea, please tell me how long you have been experiencing these symptoms and how many loose or watery stools you have passed in the last 24 hours. Additionally, have you noticed any blood, mucus, or black tarry stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Clostridioides difficile infection (C. diff). The patient has a clear risk factor (recent levofloxacin use for pneumonia) and presents with classic symptoms of acute watery diarrhea (9 episodes in 48 hours) and abdominal cramping. Please proceed to obtain a stool sample for C. difficile toxins or PCR testing.
